Pulse Wave Pitch Detection Technique and Its Application 
to Human Sensibility Evaluation 
Dong-Jun Kim 18, Hyun-Min Lee2 , Jeong-Whan Lee3 and Hang-Sik Shin4 
1Dept. of Electronic Eng., Cheongju Univ., Rep. of Korea 
21nstitute for Information & communication Technology Promotion, Rep. of Korea

adjkim@cju.ac.kr 
Keywords: Pulse Wave, Pitch Detection, Heart 
Rate Variability(HRV), Human Sensibility 
Evaluation 
Abstract. This study describes a method for 
detecting pitch of pulse wave and estimating 
Heart Rate Variability(HRV) and its relevant 
human sensibility by analyzing the information 
in terms of a pulse wave rather than of 
electrocardiogram(ECG) or electroencephalo­
gram(EEG). For this objective, pulse wave 
signals of a subject's two distinct emotional 
states (positive and negative moods) are first 
acquired. To evoke the emotions in test mode, 
the movie files in namely happy or sad mode 
are collected and played in subjects' monitor. 
From the acquired pulse signal, the features of 
HRV are calculated and consequently HRV and 
its FFT spectra are estimated to evaluate the 
human sensibility. Since a heart is an organ that 
is controlled by Autonomic Nervous System 
(ANS), ANS can reflect the variations of heart 
activity according to a person's various 
emotions. 
From the experiments it turned out that HRV 
was changed according to the subject's 
emotions. Accordingly, the sensibility 
evaluation test validated the feasibility of our 
method. 
1. Introduction 
The human sensibility ergonomics is a 
research field to evaluate human sensibility and 
to make human life more convenient and 
comfortable. Various methods for qualitative 
and quantitative evaluation of human sensibility 
have been developed and this research area 
requires understanding about the features of 
human mind and sensitivity. 
For human sensibility evaluation, biomedical 
signals such as blood pressure, electrocardio­
gram(ECG), a pulse wave, skin temperature, 
and electroencephalogram(EEG) signal are 
commonly used. Among them, EEG signal 
seems to be the most suitable to estimate human 
sensibility due to its inherent characteristics for 
representing the behavior of central nervous 
system. The most widely used biomedical 
signals for researching human sensibility 
ergonomics are EEG and ECG[l-2]. But the 
data acquisition process of EEG and ECG is 
inconvenient. There exists a crucial drawback 
of acquiring these signals and this constraint 
inhibits these signals from applying to 
ubiquitous or home healthcare systems. 
With this aim, our study presents a method 
for estimating HR V and evaluating human 
sensibility using pulse wave or photoplethys­
mogram(PPG). The PPG signals can be 
acquired more conveniently than ECG, EEG 
signals. For our objective, PPG signals for 
positive and negative emotional states are 
collected. To evoke two emotions, happy (or 
joyful) and sad (or irritating) movie files are 
chosen by each subject and they are played in 
subjects' PC monitor. From the acquired PPG 
signal, HRV is first estimated. Using the HRV 
and its FFT spectra, the human sensibility is 
evaluated. Since a heart is an organ that is 
controlled by autonomic nervous system, it may

2. HRV Estimation and Human Sensibility 
Evaluation 
2.1 Pitch Detection and HRV Estimation 
Many researches of evaluating human 
sensibility using ECG signal utilizes HRV as 
the most important feature[l-3]. The periods of 
heart beats are extracted by the peak-resolving 
and the proper post-processing techniques using 
the PPG signals. If the period is not accurate, 
HRV will show no change of sensibility. 
Therefore the period estimation is very 
important process. If accurate period is obtained, 
the period can be the same as the R-R interval 
ofECG signal and HRV can be extracted using 
the series of periods[2]. 
To determine the accurate period of heart 
beat from PPG signal, our study designed the 
peak detection technique using the heights of 
peaks, the locations of main valleys, and the 
interval of two main valleys both sides of a 
peak. The parameters used in the peak detection 
technique are shown in figure 1.

Here, H is the height of peak from the base line, 
W represents the interval of two main valleys 
both sides of a peak, and T is the period of heart 
beats. Peaks are detected in searching area in 
which the next peak can be resolved. The 
searching area is decided to be 0.25~ 1.5sec by 
our experiments. When the sign of the slope 
(derivative) is changed from positive to 
negative and the height of that point is higher 
than the predetermined threshold value, the 
point is regarded as a peak point and the 
locations and the heights of peaks, the locations 
of two neighbor valleys in each peak are 
recorded. Among the peaks that have the height 
of 95% of the highest one, the peak that has big 
valley interval is determined as the true peak. 
Periods are calculated using these true peaks. 
Finally, HRV is extracted from the sequentially 
ordered periods. The n-th HRV can be 
calculated from equation 1.

2.2 HRV- based Human Sensibility Evaluation 
To estimate the human sensibility, the 
frequency information of HRV is required, and 
power spectra of HRV can show whether the 
sympathic nerve or the parasympathic nerve is 
activated or not. Table 1 shows the criteria for 
band classification of HRV spectra.

We analyzed HRV under the criteria of the 
frequency region of HRV which is given in the 
European heart society and North American 
Society[2]. The emotional state of the subject is 
divided into positive or negative states. To 
decide the activation of the sympathic nerve or 
the parasympathic nerve, the parameter LF/HF 
is used in this study. When the LF /HF shows 
relatively big value, it is regarded that the 
parasympathic nerve is supenor to the 
sympathic nerve and the subject is under

When the LF/HF shows small value, it is

3. Experiments and Results 
3.1 Experiments 
The experiment protocol is shown in figure 3.

Figure 3. Composition of our experiment 
system 
The system is composed of a PPG acquisition 
module (FS-01 , KT-MED , Korea) , an amplifier 
and AID converter module (KBC-S02 , KT­
MED , Korea) and a personal computer. The 
PPG signal is acquired from a subject's finger 
using the PPG acquisition module. The 
amplified signal is digitized by sampling rate of 
128 samples /sec with the resolution of 12bits. 
The software for PPG data acquisition and 
sensibility evaluation is implemented using 
Visual C++ 6.0. 
Figure 4 shows the running screen for PPG 
acquisition and sensibility. Under controlled 
room temperature (23 ~26 "C ) and humidity 
(25 ~40 %) conditions, PPG signals are collected 
three times from the subjects (five males and 
two females). 
The subjects are healthy university students 
aged from 25 to 30 as shown in table 2. To 
avoid the possible influence to the nerve 
systems , subjects are requested to quit smoking, 
coffee and drinking during at least one day 
before the experiment. 
Figure 4. Running screen for PPG acquisition 
and sensibility evaluation 
Firstly, the PPG signal of resting state 1s 
collected, then the movie clip for negative 
emotion induction is played in 10 minutes and 
the PPG signal for the state is recorded . After a 
few minutes of relaxation, the movie clip for 
positive emotion induction is played in 10 
minutes and the PPG signal is recorded . The 
movie clips for negative emotion and positive 
emotion induction are selected by each subject. 
During the experiment, the initial state of the 
subjects ' emotion before the experiment and the 
self-evaluation during the experiment is 
recorded together. It seems that there is no 
relation between the self record and sensibility 
evaluation test using PPG. The assistant of the 
experiment records the states of subjects every 
20 seconds, events during the experiment.
